svg.title: Resistance of mercury near 4.2 K
svg.desc: Resistance R of a mercury sample versus temperature T from 4.1 to 4.4 K. Above 4.2 K the resistance is about 0.12 to 0.14 Ω; at 4.2 K it drops abruptly to less than 10^−5 Ω, the superconducting transition. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Cooling below the critical temperature removes electrical resistance
An idealized step illustrates mercury, not a fit to the transition width or normal-state resistance.
Current and magnetic field are assumed below their critical limits.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
